links.outcome: LLM accuracy and inter-model variability under simultaneous versus batch question delivery
links.effect: Simultaneous delivery: accuracy 38%-90% with significant inter-model differences; batches of ten: 83%-88% with no significant inter-model differences.
links.quote: When all questions were presented simultaneously, model accuracy varied widely (38%-90%), with significant inter-model differences, indicating poor reproducibility.

unlisted_practices: Structured batch delivery of prompts (reducing contextual load) to improve LLM reproducibility and reduce inter-model variability

screen.practice: structured batch delivery of prompts (reducing input context load)
screen.reason: Evaluated the effect of question delivery structure (simultaneous all-at-once vs. sequential batches of 10) on LLM reasoning stability and accuracy across six models on pediatric clinical MCQs.
